description: Unique row identifier, prefixed by mode (BUS_/TRN_/FLT_/HTL_/ACT_).
Human-readable resource category: Bus, Train, Flight, Hotel, Activity.
Same as booking_type, upper-cased, for programmatic joins with the engine's TransportMode enum.
Origin city, as given in the source dataset. Null for Hotel/Activity (location-only resources, no origin).
Destination / location city.
Indian state, from a static ~150-city lookup table. Null for cities not in that table (mostly smaller bus-route towns).
Haversine distance, computed only where BOTH cities are in the ~35-city static coordinate table. Null otherwise — not estimated, left honestly blank.
Most frequent bus operator name for this route, from the source CSV.
Top airlines serving this route (comma-separated), from the source CSV.
Sample train name(s). One row (Amritsar-Mumbai) is the real Golden Temple Mail; the rest are synthetic schedule names — see source_confidence.
Hotel name from the source listing.
Average travel duration in minutes (transport) or visit duration (activity). Null for Hotel.
No source dataset has scheduled departure times at this aggregated-by-route granularity. Kept as a column for schema completeness / future live-schedule integration, currently 100% null.
Same as departure_time — 100% null, placeholder only.
Minimum observed price for this route/class in the source data. Null for Hotel/Activity (only a single median price exists in those sources).
Median observed price (transport) or listed price (hotel/activity).
Maximum observed price. Null for Hotel/Activity, same reason as price_min_inr.
Always the literal string UNKNOWN_NO_LIVE_INVENTORY — no source has real-time inventory. Explicit placeholder, not a measured 'sold out' vs 'available' signal.
100% null — no source has seat-level inventory.
100% null — no source has room-level inventory.
Bus type (e.g. Volvo AC) or fare class (Sleeper/3A/2A/1A, Economy/Business).
Literal 'Standard (unspecified in source)' — the hotel dataset has no room-type field.
No free-text policy exists in any source; use cancellation_tier + refund_percent_* instead.
Flexible / Standard / Basic-Restrictive, assigned per-row from the source dataset's pricing band or (Hotel) directly from the source.
Best-case refund % for this cancellation_tier, joined from the real cancellation-policy table (modeled on the Himachal itinerary's actual printed policy).
Worst-case refund % for the same tier — e.g. Flexible ranges 90-100%, Basic-Restrictive ranges 0-25%.
Which of the 12 travel_disruption_scenarios.csv categories typically affect this booking_type. A static mapping, not derived per-row.
Assumed buffer (minutes) this mode can absorb before a delay becomes a missed connection. Per-mode constant (Flight=180, Train=120, Bus=90, Hotel=60, Activity=30), not measured.
0-100 baseline disruption-proneness by mode (Bus=40 highest, Hotel=10 lowest). A prior, not a per-route measurement — same value repeats within a mode.
Origin coordinates, only for the ~35 cities in the static hub table.
Origin coordinates, same coverage limit as latitude.
Destination coordinates, same coverage limit.
Destination coordinates, same coverage limit.
Google rating from the source listing.
Comma-separated amenities list from the source listing.
example_value: Breakfast, Free Wi-Fi, Free parking, Air conditioning, Bar, Restaurant, Room service, Full-service laundry, Accessible

description: Same value as price_median_inr for Hotel rows, kept as a named field for clarity in hotel-specific tooling.
Attraction category (Religious Site, Museum, etc) from the source listing.
Typical visit duration in hours, from the source listing.
Entrance fee from the source listing (0 for free sites).
Recommended time of day, from the source listing.
True if the same city pair (direction-insensitive) has more than one transport mode in this dataset — computed by cross-checking the full table, not a source field.
High/Medium/Low, a static per-mode default (Flight/Train=High since costlier to rebook, Hotel/Activity=Low) — not computed from itinerary context.
High-Verified / Medium-Verified / Low-DistanceEstimate / Low-Synthetic / Medium-Snapshot — summarizes how trustworthy THIS row's price/schedule is. See dataset_README.md for the exact rule per mode.
0-100, min-max normalized against price_median_inr WITHIN the same booking_type (and class, for Train/Flight). Cheapest in its group scores 100. Relative to this dataset only, not an absolute scale.
0-100, min-max normalized against duration_avg_min within booking_type. Fastest scores 100. Null for Hotel/Activity (no duration to compare).
0-100 per-mode constant (Flight=85 highest, Bus=50 lowest) — a prior about typical rider convenience, not measured per booking.

Currently identical to connection_risk_score — kept as a separate column because the recovery engine's ranking formula expects a risk_score field distinct from the raw connection-risk prior; the two are set equal at this build stage.
0-100, higher = lower emissions, from fixed per-mode CO2 factors (Bus=85, Train=90, Flight=20). Null for Hotel/Activity (no standard per-stay emissions factor used here).
Which raw uploaded file this row traces back to.
Boolean — True only where the row's price/schedule was checked against a real listing (e.g. HRTC fares, Golden Temple Mail), not just present in a scraped dataset.
Known or estimated vintage of the underlying data. 'Unknown'/'synthetic' where the source didn't specify a date.
